scenario.description: A college curriculum director must authorize a new dual-credit environmental science course for a partner high school and finalize its enrollment limit, course code, credit value, instructor assignment, and transcript documentation, with input from the proposed teacher, the high-school registrar, and the community-college liaison.

shared_context.S1: The partner high school has proposed a dual-credit environmental science course for the spring term.
shared_context.S2: The draft proposal lists a maximum enrollment of 28 students, three credits, and Ms. Patel as the instructor.
shared_context.S3: The course will count toward both the high-school science program and participating students' community-college transcripts.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Morgan has final authority to approve the course and its operating details.
shared_context.S5: As part of the regular curriculum-approval meeting, Dr. Morgan asks the proposed teacher, registrar, and dual-credit liaison to report any information that must be reflected before the approval is signed.

PF1.text: Ms. Patel inspected the planned laboratory room and found that the room's fixed workstations and required aisle clearance allow no more than 20 students for this course; she recorded the measurement in her classroom notes but has not yet attached it to the curriculum proposal.

PF2.text: Mr. Greene's transcript crosswalk requires this dual-credit course to use the exact course code ENV-115 and carry exactly 4 college credits; he confirmed the crosswalk with the community-college records office, but the code and credit value have not yet been entered in the high-school scheduling system.

PF3.text: The signed articulation memorandum requires Dr. Lewis to teach the first six weeks of the inaugural offering because Ms. Patel does not yet have the graduate-level coursework required for dual-credit instruction; the memorandum is filed in the liaison's partnership records but was not included with the draft proposal.

acceptance_conditions: The course must be approved with a maximum enrollment of 20 students.
The course must use course code ENV-115.
The course must carry exactly 4 college credits.
The first six weeks must be assigned to Dr. Lewis.
A commitment must record entering or updating course code ENV-115 and the 4-credit value in the scheduling system or proposal documentation.
A commitment must record the articulation memorandum and Dr. Lewis teaching the first six weeks.
The registrar's course-code and credit finding must be cited by the decision-maker.

content_checks.C5: 'Dr. Lewis' in decisions['instructor_assignment'] and 'first six weeks' in decisions['instructor_assignment']
content_checks.C6: any('ENV-115' in c['detail'] and ('4 college credits' in c['detail'] or '4-credit' in c['detail'] or 'credit value' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(('articulation memorandum' in c['detail'] or 'memorandum' in c['detail']) and 'Dr. Lewis' in c['detail'] and ('first six weeks' in c['detail'] or 'six-week' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The room inspection changes the allowable enrollment from the draft 28 students to exactly 20 students.
The transcript crosswalk changes the course code to exactly ENV-115, changes the credit value to exactly 4, and requires a matching course-code and credit update commitment.
The articulation memorandum changes the instructor for the first six weeks from Ms. Patel to Dr. Lewis and requires a commitment documenting that memorandum-based assignment.
